task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 24, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper news update on the next phase of Hallow Reed Wholesale's workweek experiment and how it separates employee schedules from customer opening days.

facts.text: Hallow Reed Wholesale announced Monday, Aug. 24, 2026, that its service counter will reopen on Fridays while many employees retain four-day schedules.
The new rotating arrangement begins Sept. 14 and is scheduled for review after six months.
A 12-week trial ran from Monday, March 16, 2026, through Friday, June 5, 2026, with the counter closed on Fridays.
Eighty participating employees worked four ten-hour days instead of five eight-hour days, with unchanged base weekly pay.
Under the new plan, employees will rotate Monday or Friday as their nonworking day so the counter can operate five days.
Employees who cannot work ten-hour days may request five eight-hour shifts; management has not published approval numbers.
Average weekly order volume during the trial was 5,400, compared with 5,000 in the preceding 12 weeks, an 8% increase.
Product mix and seasonal demand differed between those periods, so the volume comparison does not isolate a schedule effect.
Average elapsed time from order receipt to dispatch rose from 1.2 calendar days before the trial to 1.8 calendar days during it, according to the company's order log.
Customer-service logs recorded 116 Friday collection requests that had to be redirected to another day.
The logs do not show how many different customers made those requests or how many bought elsewhere.
Warehouse worker Neri Gall said the longer shifts suited his commuting arrangement but conflicted with some colleagues' evening commitments.
Gall said, "A day off is useful. So is being able to get home before the evening is gone."
Plumbing contractor Osa Keene said Friday collections often supply jobs that cannot wait until Monday.
Operations chief Torin Brack said, "Four days for a worker does not have to mean four days for the customer."
The wholesaler will add a second supervisor to the rotating counter roster without announcing new warehouse positions.
The company has not released comparable absence, overtime, profit or employee-retention figures for the trial.
The trial covered the wholesale depot, not the company's separate weekend retail outlet.
The depot distributes plumbing and electrical supplies from a building expanded in 2017.
No permanent companywide workweek policy has been adopted beyond the announced six-month arrangement.

forbidden_additions: The company abandons all four-day schedules or cuts the 40-hour base week
A causal productivity, profit or retention improvement established by the trial
